question: Do early-stage names on the incentive board, meaning a non-price incentive present (news, a material 8-K, an M&A filing (Schedule 13D, SC TO-T, 425) naming the company as its Subject, a news halt, short-dated call flow or large option prints) and a price 0-10% above the reference close, earn a positive net return over the engine's X2 one-hour hold on Alpaca paper, and more than gain-matched controls without any non-price incentive?
why_forward: Several board components have no usable history: option-trade flow is recorded from 2026-09-24 (Alpaca OPRA history starts 2024-02 and has no receive times), and halt and news receive times exist only from the monitor's first day. A prospective paper study is therefore the first honest test; it is preregistered here before any order and is never tuned on its own outcomes.

selection.order: score descending, then relative volume descending (missing last), then symbol
selection.note: The board's own stage label is not used; the gain range is checked on a fresh SIP snapshot taken after the decision time. volatility_halt (a price-triggered pause) is scored by the board but is not a non-price incentive, for selection or for the control exclusion.

controls.pool: operating companies in the same fresh full-market snapshot that pass every price, spread, dollar-volume, gain, liveness and symbol filter, are not on the board, have no non-price incentive component at the decision (monitor board.json incentive_symbols: news, mna_filing, material_8k, dilution_filing, news_halt, short_dated_calls or large_option_prints, whatever the score), and were neither selected nor used as a control by the session's other decision
controls.matching: gain bucket at the decision: [0, 3%), [3%, 6%), [6%, 10%); not matched on relative volume (a limitation)
controls.count: 4 per selected name from its gain bucket, without replacement across the whole session (both decisions)
controls.draw: ascending sha256(protocol id | session date | decision time | symbol)
controls.outcome: SIP 1-minute bars after the session: open of the first bar that starts strictly after the selection record's snapshot_completed_at, to the open of the bar 60 minutes later, less a round-trip cost of twice the cost table's half-spread for the name's cell (rules.time_bucket of the decision time, rules.price_tier of the snapshot price, rules.dv_tier of the snapshot day dollar volume) plus rules.sell_fees on the exit

execution.engine: adaptive-paper mover trial mode (blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper, merged #172); the scan's protocol field stays the engine's execution protocol mover-early-entry-v1-20260924 and its source field names this study
execution.exit: X2 (60 minutes after the first entry fill)
execution.account: isolated Alpaca paper account (alpaca-paper-2) with its own engine state root, so these sessions, sizing equity and loss budgets are not shared with other mover trials
execution.bound_code: each decision record carries the sha256 of monitor.py, board_scan.py, this protocol, the engine config, the engine files (adaptive-paper mover.py, mover_runner.py, mover_strategy.py, safety.py, runner.py, native_adapter.py, transport.py and mover-early-entry/rules.py) and the written scan, plus the running monitor's own code sha256 from board.json; it is created exclusively before the scan, so a decision cannot be re-rolled

outcomes.primary: per round trip, net return = (exit fill value - entry fill value - rules.sell_fees on the exit, fees.json sha256 fa1f468b80f78dc0c050948123116f577e38ae9f8c03f9fb360d11042a3fed3d) / entry fill value, from the engine receipt's fills; Alpaca paper charges no commission and fills at quotes, so spread cost is inside the fills
secondary: mean control-matched difference: selected model return minus the mean of its matched controls' model returns (both on the controls' outcome definition)
outcomes.session_unit: a trading day on which the study was scheduled, whatever its decisions' status; both decisions of a day belong to one session, and days whose decisions were all refused or selected nothing count as sessions without trades
outcomes.analysis_point: exactly once, after the first trading day at whose end at least 20 sessions and at least 100 completed round trips exist; no interim test is run. If a stop rule ends the study first, the same analysis runs once on the data so far and is reported as stopped early and underpowered, never as a pass
outcomes.estimator: pooled mean of per-round-trip net returns over the sessions in the sample
outcomes.test: circular block bootstrap over the n sessions in calendar order: rng = numpy.random.default_rng(int(sha256(id).hexdigest()[:16], 16)); for each of B = 20000 resamples draw k = ceil(n / 5) block starts with rng.integers(0, n, size=k), take sessions (start + j) mod n for j = 0..4 from each block in draw order, concatenate and keep the first n; the resample statistic is the pooled mean of the round trips in those sessions (sessions without trades contribute none; a resample without any round trip is dropped and counted); one-sided 95% lower bound = numpy.percentile(statistics, 5, method='linear')
outcomes.pass: lower bound > 0 and the secondary mean difference > 0

stop_rules: the engine's own lifetime gross-loss and drawdown budgets (1000 USD) and its drawdown pause (beyond 20% pauses entries for that and the next nine engine sessions)
three consecutive trading days that each end with a needs_attention receipt
any parameter or code change bound in the selection record, which starts a new protocol version instead
missed_sessions: a stale board, an early or late run, or a refused scan writes a refusal record; such decisions count as sessions without trades
gate_relation: A pass is paper performance evidence for strategy-paper-performance. The live gate also requires strategy-historical-holdout, which this study cannot supply for its history-less components; whether a preregistered forward period may stand in for that holdout is an open gate decision, not assumed here.
amendments_before_first_order: 2026-09-24, from the independent pre-outcome review (no order placed yet): volatility_halt removed from the non-price list; controls restricted to names without any non-price incentive and matched on gain bucket; the control outcome window starts after the snapshot completes; a single analysis point, estimator, bootstrap, RNG, fees and cost table fixed; rung schedule extended to 400 engine sessions and the configs pinned by sha256; code, config and scan hashes recorded before the scan; a 300 s late guard and refusal records; M&A filings credited to the subject only; monitor state restored from its files after a restart, with its start time and stream downtime recorded. Second pre-outcome review (still no order): M&A forms credited to their Subject only; volatility_halt kept out of the control exclusion list; controls without replacement across both decisions of a day; an exclusive decision ledger (no re-rolls) with refusal records for every failure; operating companies only; engine files and the running monitor's code bound in each record; the late guard re-checked after the snapshot; session, bootstrap and early-stop analysis defined exactly; halts restored after a monitor restart.
limitations: the board score is a heuristic detector fixed on 2026-09-24 without outcome data
relative volume assumes a linear volume clock, so it reads higher at 10:30 than at 13:30 for the same activity
some Benzinga articles are themselves price-driven (movers lists), so the news component is partly price-derived
session option totals and news windows depend on the monitor's uptime; restarts restore them from the monitor's files, and each record carries the monitor start time and stream downtime
paper fills are simulated by Alpaca and can differ from live fills
two decisions per session share market conditions, so sessions (not trades) are the bootstrap unit
controls are matched on the gain bucket only, not on relative volume, which selection favours
universe: operating companies only, for selection and controls: an Alpaca active tradable US equity whose symbol is in SEC company_tickers.json (dashes read as dots), is not in SEC company_tickers_mf.json (registered funds, including most ETFs), and whose Alpaca asset name has no ETF, ETN, ETP, Fund or Trust word (grantor-trust ETPs such as SPY or GLD and closed-end funds; this also excludes every operating issuer whose Alpaca name contains the whole word Trust, e.g. Northern Trust, Washington Trust Bancorp, REITs such as Federal Realty Investment Trust, and royalty trusts)
records: an append-only ledger directory: one decision record <session>-<HHMM>.json per session and decision time, created exclusively; every refusal gets its own <session>-<HHMM>-refused-<time>.json; a decision time may be retried only within its late guard, and a decision record then supersedes that time's earlier refusals (which stay in the ledger); a refusal of monitor_code_mismatch means the board did not come from the bound monitor code
schedule: decisions run only on Alpaca calendar trading days; a decision time later than that day's close minus 90 minutes is not scheduled (13:30 on early-close days), so it creates no session and no record
